criteria.criterion: The commit message or code docs name the root cause: the design's code references were not checked until the final verdict, and say how the change overlaps with reading-or-provenance-mismatch-caught-only-at-final-verdict.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The doc comment on plan::code_reference_problem says: "Root cause it addresses: the design's references to existing code were first compared with the repository at the final verdict…". It also says the queued item has the same cause, and that this check covers the item's reading half and leaves its provenance half and the item open. The CHANGELOG entry repeats both points. The plan.rs module docs and the plan_entry docs also say the check runs at plan time instead of at the final verdict.

criteria.criterion: A new test feeds a plan entry or design that names no existing code, or names a path that does not exist, and asserts it is refused or flagged before production. It fails on the pre-change code and passes with the change. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: Two tests ran and passed. plan::tests::a_design_that_names_no_existing_code_is_refused_before_production_and_says_what_is_missing covers no files, a missing path, and CHANGELOG-only, and checks that Plan::build leaves the item out of the order and records a refusal. reading::tests::a_reading_whose_design_names_no_existing_code_is_refused_at_plan_time goes through the real plan_entry with a reading that lists no deliverables or only crates/gone.rs, then through Plan::build, and asserts order is empty with a refusal. The tests use code_reference_problem, MISSING_CODE and PlanEntry::code_problem, and the diff shows all three only as additions, so the tests cannot build or pass on the base commit. On the base commit, plan_entry never sets a code problem, so such a reading would have been planned. In production, drain.rs entry_of calls reading::plan_entry with a git path lookup at head, and Plan::build then refuses the entry. So the gate does run before production on the drain path.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows a design that names existing repository paths, or states that it is wholly new code, is accepted, so the gate is not a blanket refusal. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: Two tests ran and passed. plan::tests::a_design_that_names_existing_code_or_says_it_is_wholly_new_is_accepted checks three cases: one existing file next to a created file, only created files, and a plan entry that names an existing file. Each is accepted and planned. reading::tests::a_reading_that_names_existing_code_or_is_wholly_new_passes_the_plan_check checks a Modify of an existing file, a Create-only reading, and a mix of both through plan_entry and Plan::build.

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy (all targets, no warnings), and cargo test all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for this tree: fmt passed, clippy with -D warnings passed, and cargo test --locked passed with 1469 tests.

criteria.criterion: The refusal message tells the author what is missing, e.g. which design names no existing code, in plain wording a stranger can follow.
criteria.evidence: I read the code. Plan::build now calls Refusal::lacking_because with the code_problem detail. The resulting reason reads: "the plan lacks existing code it changes or reuses; say it in the request (…) and plan again (the design names no existing code: crates/gone.rs does not exist at the base commit and is not marked as created; name the existing files it changes or reuses, or mark the new ones as created)". It names the offending paths and says how to fix the design. The plan.rs test asserts the path appears in the reason.

findings.summary: An expected deliverable was not changed: crates/athena-core/src/status.rs
findings.evidence: The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, plan.rs and reading.rs. status.rs is not on that list. No criterion needs status.rs, and refusals already reach the user through Plan.refused, so this is not a scope violation. It does leave the deliverables list unmet.

findings.summary: An item refused only for lacking code references is re-read on every plan pass, which spends budget
findings.evidence: drain treats any non-empty missing() as underspecified and re-reads the item. code_problem now adds to missing(), so a design that names a missing path is re-read before it is refused. The extra read is limited by the budget check, and the item is still refused and never produced. This only uses budget.

findings.summary: "mark the new ones as created" assumes the author knows the reading's deliverable action field
findings.evidence: The message could say outright that the deliverable's action should be create. Today it is clear enough for the Athena maintainer, who is the stated audience.

summary: The change passes. It adds a plan-time gate in athena-core: `reading::plan_entry` now sets `PlanEntry::code_problem` for a read request whose design lists no files, or lists only paths that are missing at the base commit and not marked as created. `PlanEntry::missing` and `Plan::build` then refuse the item before production, and the reason names the offending paths. The production drain path builds plan entries through `plan_entry` with a git lookup at head, so the gate runs where the request asked. I ran the four new tests and they pass. Two check refusal (one directly, one through `plan_entry` and `Plan::build`) and two check acceptance (one existing file, or only created files). They depend on symbols the diff adds, so they cannot pass on the base commit. The root cause and the overlap with reading-or-provenance-mismatch-caught-only-at-final-verdict are stated in the code docs and the CHANGELOG. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. The findings are minor: status.rs was on the expected deliverables list but was not changed (nothing needed it), and drain re-reads an item refused only for this reason before refusing it, which spends budget.
